title: President and Vice President of India

blocks.text: Part V of the Constitution is divided into 5 chapters:
Chapter I: Union Executive (President + VP + PM + COMs + Attorney General) (Art 52-78)
Chapter II: Parliament (Art 79-122)
Chapter II: Legislative powers of the President (Art 123)
Chapter IV: Union Judiciary (Art 124-147)
Chapter V: Comptroller and Auditor General of India(Art PRESIDENT OF INDIA (Article 52-62)
Article 52: There shall be a President of India, who shall be the Head of the Union Executive Article 53: Executive power of Union shall vest in President
He is the Supreme Commander of all the defence forces (Army, Navy, Airforce)
Article 54: Election of President

President is elected by an electoral college; Consisting of Elected members of both Houses of Parliament (Lok Sabha + Rajya Sabha) + Elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the States + Elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the UTs of Delhi and Puducherry.
Note: Nominated members of Parliament and Members of Legislative Council do not participate in the election of the President.
The President is:
Titular Head of the country.
First citizen of India (Ceremonial).
Nominal head / De jure head of the country.
Article 55: Manner of election
Indirect election (not directly by the people)
Proportional representation + Single Transferable Vote (STV)
Voting done by Secret ballot.
Security Deposit is = 15,000
Vote Value Calculations:
President Elections— 50 proposers + 50 seconders
Value of vote of all MLAs = (Total population of the state / Total number of elected MLAs) x 1/1000
Value of vote of an MP = Total value of votes of all MLAs /Total number of elected MPs.
He can resign by addressing the resignation letter to Vice-President.
Article 57: Eligibility for Re-election of President
Eligible for re-election any number
USA: President can of times. serve maximum of
Naturalised citizen can become
Article 58: Qualification for election as President Must be:
A citizen of India.
Minimum 35 years of age.
Qualified for election as a member of Lok Sabha.
Must not hold any office of profit. (Office of profit is not defined in the Constitution)
Office of Profit: Offices in which people are appointed and removed by the government, however offices of President, Vice President, PM, Governor are not considered as office of profit.
President is immune from any criminal 3 proceedings during his term of office.
After giving 2 months notice, civil proceedings can be carried against him.
Article 59: Conditions of office of President.
59(1) Shall not be a member of either House of Parliament or State Legislature — If he is a member, he/she should vacate the seat before appointment.
59(2) Entitled to emoluments and allowances as maybe determined by the Parliament.
59(3) Emoluments and allowances shall not be diminished during his term.
Article 60: Oath or affirmation by the President
In the presence of Chief Justice of India.
If unavailable + Senior-most judge of the Supreme Court Article 61: Procedure for impeachment of the President
Grounds of removal: violation of the Constitution. (Not defined in Constitution)
All Members of Parliament (elected + nominated) take part in the Impeachment process.
Impeachment is a removal process borrowed from USA.
Impeachment procedure:
Impeachment charges can be initiated by either house of Parliament.
Charges should be signed by 1/4 members of that House.
A 14 days notice should be given to the President.
After this the Resolution should be passed by Special Majority by both the Houses (Majority of two-thirds of the Total Membership of that House).
President has right to appear & to be represented at such investigation.
Impeachment is a Quasi-judicial process.
No President has been impeached till date.

The nominated members of either House of Parliament can participate in the impeachment of the President though they do not participate in his/her election and the elected members of the legislative assemblies of states and the Union Territories of Delhi and Puducherry do not participate in the impeachment of the President though they participate in his/her election.
Article 62: Time of holding election to fill vacancy
If term ends normally Election should be held before the expiration of President's term.
If vacancy is created due to death, resignation, removal, then:
Election must be held within 6 months, till then:
The Vice President acts as Acting President.
If Vice President is not available, then Chief Justice of India (CJI) acts as Acting President.
If CJlis also unavailable, then Senior-most Judge of the Supreme Court acts.

E.g. When President Zakir Hussain died in May 1969, the then V.P, V.V. Giri was acting as the President. When V.V Giri resigned to contest the election of President soon after, the then CJI_ M. Hidayatullah worked as the officiating President from 20th July 1969 to 24th Aug 1969.
President has the power to declare any area as Scheduled Area - Article 244(1).

Article 63: There shall be a Vice-President of India.
Post of V.P. is borrowed from U.S. Constitution.
Article 64: Vice President shall be the ex-officio Chairman of the Council of States (Rajya Sabha).
VP holds second highest constitutional post.
VP can act as President only for a maximum period of 6 months.
Article 65: Vice-President to act as President.
In the Absence of the President:
Vice President performs functions as an Acting President.
Article 66: Election of Vice-President.
All members (elected + nominated) of both Houses of Parliament (Lok Sabha + Rajya Sabha)
2. Method of Election
20 proposers + 20 electors as seconders
Voting is done through Secret Ballot.
Required Security deposit: 15,000/
Each voter has multiple preferences of voting.
3. Eligibility criteria
Must be a citizen of India
Must be of 35 years of age
Qualified for election as a member of the Rajya Sabha.
4. He shall not be a member of either house of the parliament and/or State Legislature (Same as President)
Article 67: Term of Office of Vice-President.
Can hold office upto 5 years.
Can resign to the President (and vice-versa) e.g. Jagdeep Dhankar 67(b) Removal if:
Resolution initiated (only in Rajya Sabha)
14 days prior notice required.
Passed by effective majority in RS and simple majority in LS.
Nospecific grounds is mentioned in the constitution - left to Parliament discretion.
Will continue in office until successor takes charge.
Article 68: Time of holding election to fill vacancy.
Vacancy caused due to expiration of the term of office of VP shall be completed before the expiration of the term.
If vacancy arises due to resignation, removal by Parliament, or death, then Election must be held as soon as possible.
Article 69: Oath or affirmation by Vice-President.
Administered by the President or any person appointed on behalf of him.
Article 70: Discharge of President's functions in other contingencies.
Parliament may make provisions for the discharge of the President's functions in any contingency (emergency).
Article 71: Matters relating to election of President and Vice-President.
71(1) All doubts and disputes related to elections are handled by the Supreme Court, whose decision is final (Exclusive Jurisdiction).
71(2) If election is declared void by the SC, then the acts done by VP/President before the date of declaration are considered valid.
71(3) Parliament may regulate matters related to election of President / Vice President.
71(4) Election cannot be challenged on the ground that electoral college electing that person was incomplete.
Dr.Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan and M.Hamid Ansari elected for 2 consecutive terms (Served twice as Vice President).
Longest serving VP: M. Hamid Ansari (2007-2017)
He is the only VP to serve under 3 Presidents.
Article 72: Pardoning power of the President (Judiciary Power)
Types of Pardoning Power of President:
1. Pardon—Completely removes punishment and conviction.
2. Commutation — Changes the form of punishment.
3. Remission — Reduces the punishment period.
4. Respite—Lessen the punishment due to special conditions.
5. Reprieve — Stay on execution for a temporary duration.
Q. What is the difference between the pardoning power of President and Governor?
Ans: The President can pardon death sentences and court- martial punishments while the Governor cannot. (Pardoning power of Governor is given in Article 161)
Maru Ram v. Union of India (1980):

SC held that the pardoning power of the President under Article 72 and the Governor under Article 161 is not an absolute or personal power, but must be exercised on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers and is subject to limited judicial review on grounds such as mala fide, arbitrariness, or extraneous considerations.
Kehar Singh vs Union of India Case (1988):
Pardoning power of the President is not subject to judicial review, unless the decision is arbitrary, mala fide, irrational, or discriminatory.
Judicial Powers of the President
Appoints Chief Justice and judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts.
Can seek advice from Supreme Court on any law or fact.
However, the advice tendered by the SC is not binding on him.
Exercises pardoning powers as mentioned above.
